title: ChildVox: A Speech, Audio, and Large Audio-Language Model Benchmark in Understanding and Characterizing Sound across Childhood
summary: We present ChildVox, a novel benchmark for characterizing the diverse acoustic signals through which children communicate. Specifically, ChildVox follows the full developmental trajectory from birth through school age, covering physiological sounds, non-linguistic vocalizations, canonical syllables, and spoken language. ChildVox integrates more than 20 sub-tasks across 17 child-centered audio and speech datasets, enabling systematic cross-corpus and cross-domain comparison. We evaluate a representative range of audio and speech foundation models, including self-supervised, ASR-oriented, and large audio-language models, on tasks including physiological sound classification, vocalization and canonical syllables modeling, and speech quality assessment and recognition. Benchmark results show that ChildVox provides a suite of high-performance models in recognizing a wide range of acoustic signals from children, supporting downstream applications such as characterizing children's language levels and tracking speech production with age.

AI.tldr: ChildVox is a benchmark covering children's acoustic signals from birth through school age, integrating 20+ sub-tasks across 17 datasets, and evaluating foundation models on physiological sounds, vocalizations, canonical syllables, and spoken language tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing audio/speech benchmarks lack comprehensive coverage of children's diverse acoustic signals across developmental stages, hindering systematic evaluation of models on child-centered audio tasks.
AI.method: ChildVox integrates 17 child-centered datasets with 20+ sub-tasks spanning physiological sounds, non-linguistic vocalizations, canonical syllables, and spoken language; evaluates self-supervised, ASR-oriented, and large audio-language models.
AI.result: ChildVox demonstrates high-performance model recognition across children's acoustic signals, enabling downstream applications like language level characterization and age-tracking of speech production.
AI.conclusion: ChildVox provides a unified benchmark for child audio analysis, enabling systematic cross-corpus comparisons and supporting developmental speech and language research.

title: Audio Deepfake Detection with Half-Truth Localisation Using Cross-Attentive Feature Fusion
summary: Audio deepfake detection is well-studied as a binary problem, but partially manipulated speech, where a short synthesised segment is spliced into an otherwise genuine utterance, poses a harder and more realistic threat. Detecting such half-truth audio requires not only distinguishing it from real and fully fake speech, but also localising where the manipulation occurs. We present CAFNet, a 576k-parameter architecture that addresses both tasks jointly: it performs ternary classification (real, fully-fake, or half-truth) and regresses the temporal boundaries of the synthesised region in a single forward pass. CAFNet fuses Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC), Linear-Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (LFCC), and Chroma Short-Time Fourier Transform (Chroma-STFT) features through parallel depthwise-separable convolution branches with cross-attention, followed by a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) regression head for boundary prediction. On the combined Multi-Lingual Audio Deepfake Detection Corpus (MLADDC) T2+T3 test set, CAFNet achieves 92.71% accuracy and macro Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9910, with boundary localisation Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.075s and a median error of 0.052s. On binary detection, it achieves 96.76% accuracy and 3.20% Equal Error Rate (EER), outperforming fine-tuned XLS-R 300M (78.31%) and AST 87M (93.03%) at over 500 times fewer parameters. A cross-dataset study further shows that standard fine-tuning collapses cross-domain representations even under reduced backbone learning rates.

AI.tldr: CAFNet is a lightweight 576k-parameter model for detecting and localizing partially manipulated (half-truth) audio. It jointly performs ternary classification (real, fully-fake, half-truth) and temporal boundary regression, achieving state-of-the-art results on the MLADDC dataset while being over 500x smaller than prior models like XLS-R and AST.
AI.motivation: Existing audio deepfake detection research focuses on binary classification (real vs. fake), but partially manipulated speech—where a short synthesized segment is spliced into genuine audio—is a more realistic and challenging threat. Detecting such half-truth audio requires both distinguishing it from real and fully fake speech and localizing the manipulated region, which prior work has not jointly addressed.
AI.method: CAFNet fuses three feature representations (MFCC, LFCC, Chroma-STFT) using parallel depthwise-separable convolution branches with cross-attention, followed by a BiLSTM regression head for boundary prediction. The model performs both ternary classification (real, fully-fake, half-truth) and temporal boundary regression in a single forward pass.
AI.result: On the MLADDC T2+T3 test set: 92.71% accuracy, macro AUC 0.9910, boundary localization MAE of 0.075s and median error 0.052s. On binary detection: 96.76% accuracy and 3.20% EER, outperforming XLS-R 300M (78.31%) and AST 87M (93.03%) with over 500x fewer parameters.
AI.conclusion: CAFNet is an efficient and effective solution for partial audio manipulation detection and localization. The cross-dataset study also reveals that standard fine-tuning collapses cross-domain representations even with reduced backbone learning rates, highlighting a robustness challenge in deepfake detection.

title: COMET: Concept Space Dissection of the Modality Gap in Audio-Text Multimodal Contrastive Embeddings
summary: Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining (CLAP) models are widely used for audio understanding and support modality-agnostic condition swapping in many zero-shot applications. However, their performance is heavily affected by the modality gap between audio and text embeddings. Existing explanations mainly attribute this gap to the cone effect, treating it as a shift between mean embeddings, yet correcting the mean alone yields only limited improvements. Alternative hypotheses, such as information imbalance and dimensionality collapse, have also been proposed, but they remain insufficiently verified and have not been thoroughly studied in the audio domain. Meanwhile, several works attempt to decompose multimodal contrastive embeddings into interpretable concepts, but none explicitly analyze the modality gap from the perspective of concept decomposition. In this work, we introduce COMET (Concept space Organization and Modality gap Explanation with PLS-SVD Transformation), a novel partial least squares singular value decomposition (PLS-SVD) framework for CLAP that unveils a broader perspective of the modality gap. Our framework reveals that only a small, interpretable subset of axes, which captures shared concepts, contributes substantially to similarity computation, and that the mean component represents only partially the modality gap. Building on this insight, we propose a simple spectral truncation method that mitigates the modality gap in a training-free manner. The method enables zero-shot audio captioning with condition swapping to approach fully supervised performance, without requiring large auxiliary memory banks or expensive computation. At the same time, it achieves substantial embedding dimensionality reduction while preserving strong performance on retrieval and audio captioning tasks.

AI.tldr: COMET introduces a PLS-SVD framework to analyze the modality gap in CLAP models, revealing that only a few interpretable concept axes contribute to similarity. A simple spectral truncation method mitigates the gap in a training-free manner, enabling zero-shot audio captioning to approach supervised performance while reducing embedding dimensionality.
AI.motivation: Existing explanations of the modality gap in CLAP (e.g., cone effect, information imbalance) are insufficient and have not been thoroughly studied in the audio domain. No prior work has analyzed the gap from the perspective of concept decomposition.
AI.method: Proposes COMET, a PLS-SVD framework that decomposes multimodal contrastive embeddings to reveal that only a small, interpretable subset of axes (shared concepts) contributes substantially to similarity. Introduces a training-free spectral truncation method to mitigate the modality gap.
AI.result: Zero-shot audio captioning with condition swapping approaches fully supervised performance without auxiliary memory banks or expensive computation. Achieves substantial embedding dimensionality reduction while maintaining strong performance on retrieval and audio captioning tasks.
AI.conclusion: The modality gap in CLAP can be effectively explained and mitigated through concept decomposition via PLS-SVD, and simple spectral truncation offers a practical, training-free solution.

title: HoliTok:A Coutinuous Holistic Tokenization with Robust Dual Capabilities of Speech Generation and Understanding
summary: Unified speech foundation models require a holistic tokenization space that is both learnable by language models and decodable into high-quality waveforms. Existing speech tokenizers, however, often fail to satisfy these requirements simultaneously, leading to increased architectural complexity and more involved training designs. We propose HoliTok, a continuous Holistic speech Tokenization model designed for unified generation-understanding modeling. HoliTok encodes 48~kHz speech into a compact 25~Hz sequence of 128-dimensional latents. It is trained with a progressive strategy that jointly preserves signal-level fidelity, incorporates semantic information, and maintains strong latent learnability. Based on this tokenization, we build a unified AR+DiT model for speech synthesis and recognition, where the same latent sequence supports both generation-specific and unified generation-understanding tasks. Experiments show that HoliTok achieves competitive reconstruction fidelity, improves generative learnability for high-quality and controllable synthesis, and, among the evaluated representations, is the only one that operates robustly in our unified generation-understanding architecture without additional optimization tricks. These results suggest that HoliTok serves as an effective speech tokenizer and a foundational representation interface for unified spoken language modeling. The code is available at: https://github.com/bovod-sjtu/HoliTok.

AI.tldr: HoliTok is a continuous holistic speech tokenization model that encodes 48kHz speech into compact 25Hz 128-dimensional latents, achieving high reconstruction fidelity, generative learnability, and robust performance in unified generation-understanding architectures without additional optimization tricks.
AI.motivation: Existing speech tokenizers fail to simultaneously provide a tokenization space that is both learnable by language models and decodable into high-quality waveforms, leading to increased architectural complexity and more involved training designs for unified speech foundation models.
AI.method: HoliTok encodes 48kHz speech into a compact 25Hz sequence of 128-dimensional latents using a progressive training strategy that jointly preserves signal-level fidelity, incorporates semantic information, and maintains strong latent learnability. A unified AR+DiT model is built where the same latent sequence supports both generation-specific and unified generation-understanding tasks.
AI.result: HoliTok achieves competitive reconstruction fidelity, improves generative learnability for high-quality and controllable synthesis, and among evaluated representations, it is the only one that operates robustly in the unified generation-understanding architecture without additional optimization tricks.
AI.conclusion: HoliTok serves as an effective speech tokenizer and a foundational representation interface for unified spoken language modeling.

title: The WER Trap: Shattering the Illusion of Unified Tokens in Speech Language Models
summary: The pursuit of a "unified" discrete token for both speech understanding and generation has led the Speech Language Model (SLM) community to heavily rely on Word Error Rate (WER) -- the core metric for Whisper-style tokenizers -- as the definitive proxy for representation quality. This fosters the assumption that low-WER tokens inherently preserve the information necessary for intelligible acoustic synthesis. We argue this is fundamentally deceptive. While high-frequency tokens succeed in generation tasks due to implicit information leakage, isolating pure semantic information at ultra-low frame rates strips away the finegrained articulation and micro-dynamics essential for ODE-based generation. Empirically validating this requires extreme compression without sacrificing WER -- a methodological bottleneck, as standard fixed-stride downsampling arbitrarily truncates phonetic boundaries. To overcome this, we develop a dynamic compression tokenizer that intelligently aligns representations with semantic boundaries, achieving ultra-low frame rates with exceptionally low WER. Using these isolated "pure" semantic tokens, we expose the WER trap: when conditioning generative models -- even with oracle duration alignments -- the reconstructed speech suffers from severe articulation blur and is rendered acoustically unintelligible. Our findings demonstrate that semantic categorization rewarded by low WER is inherently orthogonal to the continuous phonetic trajectories required for synthesis, shattering the illusion of the unified token and advocating for explicitly decoupled speech representations.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the assumption that low Word Error Rate (WER) tokens from Whisper-style tokenizers are sufficient for both speech understanding and generation. The authors develop a dynamic compression tokenizer that achieves ultra-low frame rates with low WER, then show that conditioning generative models on these "pure" semantic tokens produces acoustically unintelligible speech, proving that semantic categorization and phonetic generation require decoupled representations.
AI.motivation: The SLM community assumes low-WER tokens (from Whisper-style tokenizers) serve as a unified representation for both speech understanding and generation. The authors argue this is deceptive because low-WER semantic tokens, when isolated via extreme compression, strip away the fine-grained articulation and micro-dynamics essential for ODE-based acoustic synthesis, revealing an inherent orthogonality between semantic categorization and continuous phonetic trajectories.
AI.method: The authors develop a dynamic compression tokenizer that aligns representations with semantic boundaries (rather than fixed-stride downsampling), achieving ultra-low frame rates with exceptionally low WER. They then condition ODE-based generative models on these isolated "pure" semantic tokens (with oracle duration alignments) and evaluate the acoustic intelligibility of reconstructed speech.
AI.result: Even with oracle duration alignments, generative models conditioned on low-WER pure semantic tokens produce speech with severe articulation blur that is acoustically unintelligible. This empirically demonstrates that semantic categorization (rewarded by low WER) is orthogonal to the continuous phonetic trajectories required for synthesis.
AI.conclusion: The notion of a unified discrete token for both speech understanding and generation is an illusion. The authors advocate for explicitly decoupled speech representations — separate representations for semantic content (understanding) and phonetic/acoustic detail (generation).

title: Identifiability of Low Frequency Li-ion Battery Parameters in Time Domain
summary: This paper investigates the identification of observable low-frequency (LF) parameters of battery cell's equivalent circuit models (ECMs) using time-domain voltage and current measurements sampled at low frequency by built-in battery management systems (BMS) during operation. Accurate estimation of such parameters is challenging due to measurement resolution available in practical settings. To address this, a modeling and identification framework is proposed in which fractional constant phase element (CPE), commonly used to model LF diffusion phenomena of battery cells, is approximated in the time domain using a high-order RC network with a recursive definition. The parameter estimation problem is formulated as a constrained, non-convex least-squares problem in a discretized state-space representation. To improve robustness, parameter initialization strategies, bounds, and a procedure for selecting the number of RC branches are rigorously derived. The method is evaluated in a numerical study based on a power system application where the battery under the study provides primary frequency control to the grid. Under noise levels representative of typical BMS measurements, the proposed approach achieves, from time-domain measurements, accurate LF parameter estimation (including the CPE), with average errors below 1 %.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a framework for identifying low-frequency parameters of battery ECMs (including fractional CPE) from low-sampling-rate BMS measurements, using a high-order RC network approximation and constrained non-convex least-squares optimization, achieving <1% average estimation error in a grid frequency control application.
AI.motivation: Accurate estimation of observable low-frequency parameters of battery ECMs is challenging due to limited measurement resolution in practical BMS settings, yet these parameters are critical for applications like grid frequency control.
AI.method: A time-domain approximation of fractional CPE via a recursively-defined high-order RC network; parameter estimation formulated as a constrained non-convex least-squares problem in discretized state-space; rigorous derivation of initialization strategies, bounds, and RC branch selection procedure.
AI.result: Under typical BMS noise levels, the proposed method achieves accurate LF parameter estimation (including CPE) with average errors below 1% in a numerical study of primary frequency control.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework enables reliable low-frequency ECM parameter identification from low-sampling-rate, noisy BMS measurements, supporting practical battery modeling for power system applications.

title: Audio Jailbreaks in Large Audio-Language Models: Taxonomy, Attack-Defense Analysis, and Cost-Aware Evaluation
summary: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) expand jailbreak risks from token-level prompting to the full speech perception-to-reasoning pipeline, where unsafe behavior can be induced through semantics, acoustic style, signal artifacts, or internal representations. Existing work studies these risks under heterogeneous threat models and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to compare attack practicality or defense utility. This paper provides a unified taxonomy and a controlled empirical evaluation of LALM jailbreak attacks and defenses. We organize prior work into semantic, acoustic, signal, and embedding-layer attacks; guard-based, training-free, and training-based defenses; and cross-modal, audio-native, and interactive benchmarks. We then evaluate representative attacks and defenses across ten open-source LALMs, measuring not only attack success rate but also benign refusal and latency. Our results show that Acoustic Best-of-N reveals strong worst-case audio-space vulnerabilities, Narrative Framing is an effective low-latency semantic threat, and current defenses trade robustness against benign usability. These findings support cost- and utility-aware evaluation as a necessary complement to success-rate-only LALM safety benchmarks.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a unified taxonomy and controlled empirical evaluation of jailbreak attacks and defenses in Large Audio Language Models (LALMs), covering semantic, acoustic, signal, and embedding-layer attacks; guard-based, training-free, and training-based defenses; and three benchmark types. Evaluating ten open-source LALMs reveals that Acoustic Best-of-N exposes strong audio-space vulnerabilities, Narrative Framing is an effective low-latency semantic threat, and current defenses trade robustness against benign usability, highlighting the need for cost- and utility-aware evaluation beyond success-rate-only metrics.
AI.motivation: Existing work on LALM jailbreak risks suffers from heterogeneous threat models and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to compare attack practicality or defense utility. This paper aims to unify the field with a consistent taxonomy and controlled empirical evaluation.
AI.method: The authors organize prior work into a unified taxonomy: attacks across semantic, acoustic, signal, and embedding layers; defenses as guard-based, training-free, and training-based; benchmarks as cross-modal, audio-native, and interactive. They then conduct controlled empirical evaluations of representative attacks and defenses across ten open-source LALMs, measuring attack success rate, benign refusal, and latency.
AI.result: Acoustic Best-of-N reveals strong worst-case audio-space vulnerabilities. Narrative Framing is an effective low-latency semantic threat. Current defenses trade robustness against benign usability. Success-rate-only metrics are insufficient; cost- and utility-aware evaluation is necessary.
AI.conclusion: The paper advocates for cost- and utility-aware evaluation as a necessary complement to success-rate-only LALM safety benchmarks, given the observed trade-offs between defense robustness and benign usability.

title: Decoding Strategies for Diffusion-Based ASR: A Systematic Evaluation of Confidence-Based Thresholding
summary: While LLM-based Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) achieves high accuracy, its speed is limited by sequential autoregressive decoding. Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer a parallel alternative, yet their decoding strategies remain under-explored in ASR contexts. This paper analyzes three decoding schemes for DLM-based ASR: fixed-number, static confidence threshold, and dynamic confidence threshold. We propose measuring round-wise accuracy using Negative Log-Likelihood-based uncertainty as a proxy for decoding progress. Our results show that both threshold-based strategies significantly outperform fixed-number schemes in accuracy and speed. We attribute this to a property unique to ASR: most tokens reach high confidence early, allowing reliable ones to be harvested aggressively while leaving only difficult tokens for later rounds. Notably, the static-threshold strategy matches the accuracy of autoregressive decoding while offering superior efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes three decoding schemes for DLM-based ASR, finding that threshold-based strategies (static and dynamic confidence) outperform fixed-number decoding in both accuracy and speed, with static-threshold matching autoregressive accuracy while being more efficient.
AI.motivation: DLM-based ASR decoding strategies are under-explored; existing fixed-number schemes are suboptimal.
AI.method: Analyzes three decoding schemes: fixed-number, static confidence threshold, and dynamic confidence threshold; uses NLL-based uncertainty as a proxy for decoding progress.
AI.result: Threshold-based strategies significantly outperform fixed-number schemes; static-threshold matches autoregressive accuracy with superior efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Most tokens reach high confidence early in ASR, enabling aggressive early harvesting of reliable tokens and focused decoding on difficult ones.

title: Tensorized Radiative Heat Transfer for a Scalable and Calibrated Building Energy Simulator
summary: Accurate building energy simulation is essential for developing advanced control strategies that enable demand flexibility and grid responsiveness. The Smart Buildings Control Suite (sbsim) offers a lightweight, scalable, and data-calibrated simulation environment based on a tensorized finite difference model. Previous work extended sbsim to include interior long-wave radiative heat exchange between indoor surfaces. However, a complete thermal model must also account for exterior radiative processes, including long-wave radiation exchange with the sky and surroundings, as well as short-wave solar radiation incident on building surfaces. This paper presents a comprehensive radiative heat transfer implementation for sbsim that integrates both interior and exterior radiation mechanisms. Our primary contribution is the development and integration of a fully tensorized exterior radiation module that captures sky and ground long-wave exchange as well as solar heat gains through opaque and transparent surfaces. By formulating these processes as tensor operations compatible with the existing framework, we preserve the computational efficiency necessary for reinforcement learning applications. We validate our implementation against established simulation tools and demonstrate improved prediction accuracy for surface temperatures and building thermal loads. This enhancement significantly increases the physical fidelity of sbsim, enabling more realistic training environments for building energy optimization and control.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a comprehensive radiative heat transfer implementation for the sbsim building simulation environment, integrating both interior and exterior radiation mechanisms (including sky/ground long-wave exchange and solar radiation) as tensor operations compatible with reinforcement learning applications, validated against established tools.
AI.motivation: Accurate building energy simulation is needed for advanced control strategies enabling demand flexibility and grid responsiveness. The existing sbsim environment lacked exterior radiative processes (long-wave sky/ground exchange and short-wave solar radiation), limiting its physical fidelity.
AI.method: The authors developed and integrated a fully tensorized exterior radiation module capturing sky and ground long-wave exchange and solar heat gains through opaque and transparent surfaces, formulated as tensor operations compatible with the existing sbsim framework.
AI.result: Validation against established simulation tools showed improved prediction accuracy for surface temperatures and building thermal loads.
AI.conclusion: The enhancement significantly increases the physical fidelity of sbsim, enabling more realistic training environments for building energy optimization and control, particularly for reinforcement learning applications.

title: MELD: Mel-Spectrogram-Based Speech Language Modeling with Discrete Latent Variables
summary: Recent speech language models rely on encoders that are optimized separately from autoregressive models. Since these encoders are unaware of the downstream objectives, the extracted representations may not be optimal for downstream tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce a discrete latent variable model on mel spectrograms that jointly optimizes the encoder and the speech language model. Joint optimization not only brings improvements over codec-based and other mel-spectrogram-based baselines on zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Speech-to-Text (STT) tasks, but also effectively alleviates common issues in autoregressive mel-spectrogram modeling, such as prolonged silence generation and word omissions.

AI.tldr: A discrete latent variable model on mel spectrograms with joint optimization of encoder and speech language model improves zero-shot TTS and STT tasks while reducing issues like prolonged silence and word omissions.
AI.motivation: Speech language models use encoders optimized separately from autoregressive models, causing suboptimal representations for downstream tasks.
AI.method: Introduces a discrete latent variable model on mel spectrograms that jointly optimizes the encoder and the speech language model.
AI.result: Improvements over codec-based and mel-spectrogram-based baselines on zero-shot TTS and STT tasks; alleviates prolonged silence generation and word omissions.
AI.conclusion: Joint optimization of encoder and speech language model via discrete latent variables yields better performance and mitigates common autoregressive mel-spectrogram modeling issues.

title: Local Observability and Moving Horizon Estimation-based Training of Feedforward Neural Networks
summary: In this paper, we propose a moving horizon estimation (MHE)-based training method for feedforward neural networks (FNNs) with rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation functions to determine their ideal weights from a control-theoretic perspective. This allows for a rigorous theoretical analysis of the trained network. First, we reformulate the FNN as a dynamical system with the weights as states. Then, we investigate the local observability of such a system. For two-layer FNNs with fixed output weights, we derive a sufficient condition under which the observability rank condition holds, ensuring a locally observable state. We also show that multi-layer FNNs in general fail to satisfy the observability rank condition. Based on this analysis, we develop a persistently exciting (PE) input design method, which renders a state distinguishable from its neighbors. The resulting local observability provides convergence guarantees for the proposed MHE-based training, where only the projection of the state onto the observable subspace is updated using a fixed-length window of input-output data. The effectiveness of the approach is illustrated via numerical examples.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a moving horizon estimation (MHE)-based training method for ReLU feedforward neural networks, treating weight optimization as a dynamical system observability problem. It establishes local observability conditions for two-layer FNNs, designs persistently exciting inputs, and provides convergence guarantees for the MHE-based training approach.
AI.motivation: To provide a control-theoretic perspective for training ReLU FNNs with rigorous theoretical analysis, convergence guarantees, and observability-based weight estimation rather than conventional gradient-based methods.
AI.method: Reformulates FNN as a dynamical system with weights as states; analyzes local observability via observability rank condition; develops persistently exciting (PE) input design; applies MHE to update only the observable subspace projection using fixed-length windows of input-output data.
AI.result: For two-layer FNNs with fixed output weights, a sufficient condition for observability rank condition is derived. Multi-layer FNNs generally fail the observability rank condition. The PE input design ensures state distinguishability, and MHE-based training achieves convergence guarantees.
AI.conclusion: The MHE-based training method offers a theoretically grounded alternative for training ReLU FNNs with provable convergence, leveraging control-theoretic observability and PE input design, as validated by numerical examples.

title: Mitigating Stethoscope-Induced Shortcuts in Respiratory Sound Classification under Federated Domain Generalization with Causality-Inspired Interventions
summary: AI-driven respiratory sound classification (RSC) is promising for automated pulmonary disease detection, yet multi-site deployment is hindered by inter-stethoscope variability. We introduce a federated domain generalization (FedDG) formulation for RSC under stethoscope-induced device shifts, where clients use heterogeneous devices and the model is evaluated on unseen devices. Our empirical analysis shows that stethoscope-induced style and disease-specific content are tightly entangled, making deterministic style removal unreliable. In response, we propose a causality-inspired multimodal FedDG framework that combines: (i) a causality-inspired device style intervention network that performs content-preserving style perturbations, (ii) counterfactual text augmentation that neutralizes metadata shortcuts, and (iii) gradient alignment that facilitates device-invariant representations across clients. Built on a multimodal language-audio pretraining model, it outperforms conventional data augmentation and federated learning baselines in leave-one-device-out validation on ICBHI and SPRSound datasets. Code will be released upon publication.

AI.tldr: Proposes a causality-inspired multimodal federated domain generalization framework for respiratory sound classification that handles inter-stethoscope variability via style intervention, counterfactual text augmentation, and gradient alignment, outperforming baselines on ICBHI and SPRSound datasets.
AI.motivation: Multi-site deployment of AI-driven respiratory sound classification is hindered by inter-stethoscope variability (device shifts), and existing deterministic style removal approaches fail because stethoscope-induced style and disease-specific content are tightly entangled.
AI.method: A causality-inspired multimodal federated domain generalization (FedDG) framework with three components: (i) a device style intervention network for content-preserving style perturbations, (ii) counterfactual text augmentation to neutralize metadata shortcuts, and (iii) gradient alignment for device-invariant representations across clients. Built on a multimodal language-audio pretraining model.
AI.result: Outperforms conventional data augmentation and federated learning baselines in leave-one-device-out validation on ICBHI and SPRSound datasets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed FedDG approach effectively addresses device-induced domain shifts in respiratory sound classification, and code will be released upon publication.

title: Grid Capacity Expansion under Data Centers and Electrified Manufacturing Large Loads
summary: In this paper, we consider the expansion of power grids under emerging large loads from data centers and electrified manufacturing. We develop a multi-period grid capacity expansion model to determine optimal investment profiles for power generation, storage, and transmission capacity while accounting for hourly power dispatch, such that electricity demand is satisfied and the total planning and operation cost is minimized. We also propose a new modeling approach regarding the spatial distribution of demand from large loads. The model is used to analyze the expansion of a synthetic grid that follows key characteristics of the ERCOT system over a seven-year planning horizon, under loads from data centers and electrified oil refining, which account for 17.5% and 4.7% of total annual electricity demand by the end of the planning horizon. The optimal investment policy leads to an 83.6% increase in generation capacity and exploits the short construction times of solar and storage as well as the operational flexibility of thermal generators. Finally, sensitivity analysis reveals that the construction time of grid assets substantially impacts investment timing, generation technology mix, and transmission capacity expansion. The proposed modeling framework is general and can be extended to other grid systems, enabling the exploration of diverse demand scenarios, policy assumptions, and regional characteristics.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a multi-period grid capacity expansion model to optimize investment in power generation, storage, and transmission under emerging large loads from data centers and electrified manufacturing, using a synthetic ERCOT-like grid over seven years. Results show an 83.6% generation capacity increase, with solar, storage, and thermal flexibility playing key roles, while construction time significantly impacts investment decisions.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by the need to expand power grids to accommodate rapidly growing large loads from data centers and electrified manufacturing, which pose new challenges for grid planning and investment.
AI.method: A multi-period grid capacity expansion model is developed, incorporating hourly power dispatch and a novel spatial distribution approach for large loads, to minimize total planning and operation costs.
AI.result: Optimal investment leads to an 83.6% increase in generation capacity; solar and storage exploit short construction times, and thermal generators provide operational flexibility. Construction time of grid assets substantially impacts investment timing, technology mix, and transmission expansion.
AI.conclusion: The modeling framework is general and extensible to other grid systems, enabling exploration of diverse demand scenarios, policy assumptions, and regional characteristics.

title: Frequency-Modulated and Single-Tone Excitation to Reveal Vibro-Acoustic Nonlinearities in Loosened Bolted Joints
summary: Preload loss in bolted joints results in alterations of the stiffness, damping, and nonlinearity of the structure, but existing monitoring techniques for rail-vehicle systems are often not capable of combining controlled shaker tests and sensing of nonlinear features. This paper proposes a method for detecting bolt loosening using a vibro-acoustic technique, where the structure is subjected to controlled shaker tests to sense the nonlinear features. A triaxial accelerometer was attached to the demonstrator, a microphone was placed in close proximity, and one of the bolts was tested under 0%, 20%, 40%, and 80% preload conditions. Single-tone and frequency-modulated (FM) signals close to the main natural frequency of 130 Hz, which was identified using sine sweep and narrow-band excitation, were applied to the demonstrator. When the structure was subjected to 130 Hz single-tone excitation, the loose state of the bolt exhibited several additional high-frequency spectral peaks. FM excitation between 125 and 135 Hz further distinguished between the states. Harmonic band power ratios, normalized to the carrier, distinguished between the loose state and the 80% preload state, where the difference between the loose and 80% preload states was 17.5 dB for l = 2 and 36.5 dB for l = 6.

AI.tldr: A vibro-acoustic method using controlled shaker tests and nonlinear feature sensing (harmonic band power ratios) detects bolt preload loss (0-80%) by analyzing spectral peaks from 130 Hz single-tone and FM excitation, achieving up to 36.5 dB distinction between loose and preloaded states.
AI.motivation: Existing monitoring techniques for rail-vehicle bolted joints cannot effectively combine controlled shaker tests with sensing of nonlinear features to detect preload loss, which alters stiffness, damping, and nonlinearity.
AI.method: A triaxial accelerometer and microphone were used on a demonstrator with one bolt tested at 0%, 20%, 40%, and 80% preload. Sine sweep identified the main natural frequency (~130 Hz). Single-tone (130 Hz) and FM (125-135 Hz) excitations were applied. Harmonic band power ratios normalized to the carrier were computed to distinguish preload states.
AI.result: Single-tone excitation at 130 Hz produced additional high-frequency spectral peaks under loose conditions. FM excitation between 125-135 Hz further distinguished states. The loose vs. 80% preload difference was 17.5 dB (l=2) and 36.5 dB (l=6) in harmonic band power ratio.
AI.conclusion: The vibro-acoustic technique with harmonic band power ratio analysis effectively detects bolt loosening severity in bolted joints, offering a quantitative metric for preload loss monitoring.

title: Energy-Optimal Thermal Management of Heat-Pump Battery Electric Vehicles
comment: This paper has been submitted for publication in IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology (OJVT)
summary: This paper presents an energy-optimal hybrid control framework for thermal management of heat-pump battery electric vehicles (BEVs). The controller coordinates the compressor, coolant pumps, and cabin blower across the coupled refrigerant, coolant, and air loops, while enforcing cabin comfort and component temperature constraints. The framework combines a rule-based supervisory layer, which handles discrete system configuration, with a continuous nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) optimizer that minimizes thermal energy consumption over a finite prediction horizon. A control-oriented model is developed to capture the dominant dynamics of the cabin, refrigerant loop, reconfigurable coolant circuits, and key thermal masses including the battery, motor, and inverter. The model is validated against a high-fidelity reference, achieving a mean absolute temperature prediction error below \SI{1.8}{\celsius} for key thermal states including the battery, motor, and cabin air temperature, while reducing simulation time by approximately \SI{85}{\percent}. The terminal cost is computed by linearizing the system about a quasi-steady operating point and solving the discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation, ensuring well-conditioned optimization across varying operating conditions. The proposed framework is evaluated against the built-in rule-based controller of MathWorks Simscape \emph{Electric Vehicle Thermal Management with Heat Pump} model under cold-climate extended driving conditions, demonstrating consistent reductions of \SI{20}{}-\SI{28}{\percent} in thermal energy consumption across all tested scenarios. The complete implementation, developed using the open-source CasADi framework, is made openly available at \href{https://github.com/PrashantLokur/ThermalEnergyManagementWithHybridControlFramework}{GitHub} repository to support reproducibility and further development.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid control framework combining rule-based supervisory logic with nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) for thermal management of heat-pump battery electric vehicles. The approach reduces thermal energy consumption by 20–28% against a baseline rule-based controller across cold-climate driving scenarios, validated on a high-fidelity Simscape model.
AI.motivation: Thermal management in BEVs—coordinating the compressor, pumps, and blower across multiple coupled loops (refrigerant, coolant, air)—is a complex and energy-intensive task. Existing rule-based controllers are suboptimal, and there is a need for a control framework that systematically minimizes thermal energy consumption while enforcing comfort and component temperature constraints.
AI.method: A hybrid control framework is developed: (1) a rule-based supervisory layer handles discrete system configuration (e.g., circuit routing, mode switching); (2) a continuous NMPC optimizer minimizes thermal energy consumption over a finite horizon. A control-oriented model capturing cabin, refrigerant, coolant, and key thermal masses (battery, motor, inverter) is validated against a high-fidelity model (mean error < 1.8°C, 85% simulation time reduction). Terminal cost is computed via linearization and discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation (DARE) to ensure well-conditioned optimization.
AI.result: The proposed framework consistently reduces thermal energy consumption by 20–28% compared to the built-in rule-based controller of MathWorks Simscape Electric Vehicle Thermal Management with Heat Pump model under cold-climate extended driving scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid control framework significantly outperforms traditional rule-based thermal management for heat-pump BEVs, offering substantial energy savings while maintaining cabin comfort and component safety. The open-source release supports reproducibility and further research.

title: Distributed Non-Uniform Scaling Control of Multi-Agent Formation with Dynamic Agent Joining
comment: This paper has been accepted by IFAC 2026
summary: Non-uniform scaling control of formation enables multi-agent systems to adjust their shape by scaling with different ratios along different coordinate axes, offering enhanced flexibility in complex environments. However, like most existing formation maneuver strategies, it typically assumes a fixed set of agents, limiting its applicability in scenarios requiring dynamic team expansion. This paper introduces a distributed control framework that enables a formation to incorporate new agents during non-uniform scaling maneuvers in arbitrary dimensions while preserving the spectral properties of the graph Laplacian. Simulation examples validate the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

AI.tldr: A distributed control framework for multi-agent formations that allows dynamic addition of agents during non-uniform scaling maneuvers while preserving graph Laplacian spectral properties.
AI.motivation: Existing formation maneuver strategies, including non-uniform scaling control, assume a fixed set of agents, limiting their use in scenarios requiring dynamic team expansion.
AI.method: A distributed control framework that enables incorporation of new agents during non-uniform scaling maneuvers in arbitrary dimensions while preserving the spectral properties of the graph Laplacian.
AI.result: Simulation examples validate the effectiveness of the theoretical results.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully extends non-uniform scaling formation control to accommodate dynamic team expansion.

title: Closed-Loop Identification of Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation
summary: This paper studies closed-loop identification of linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants, with emphasis on open-loop unstable plants for which open-loop experiments are not practically available. The central contribution is an exact algebraic plant-extraction theorem for cycled closed-loop realizations: for square strictly proper plants and a controller path satisfying an invertibility condition, the cycled plant transfer matrix is recovered from a shared state-space realization of the stable closed-loop maps from the external reference to the plant output and to the control input, without state augmentation, and without requiring the recovered plant realization to be stable. Thus, the stability requirement for data generation is shifted from the open-loop plant to the internally stable closed-loop system. Building on this result, a closed-loop identification algorithm is constructed that takes the reference, output, and input signals as data, applies standard subspace identification to the cycled signals, performs the algebraic plant extraction, and recovers the LPTV plant state-space parameters via a coordinate transformation; the conditioning of the inverse controller path governs the reliability of the extraction step. Numerical examples demonstrate the recovery of stable and open-loop unstable SISO LPTV plants and validate a MIMO case through coordinate-invariant Markov-parameter comparisons.

AI.tldr: A closed-loop identification method for LPTV plants (including open-loop unstable ones) using an algebraic plant-extraction theorem from stable cycled closed-loop realizations, without requiring open-loop experiments or state augmentation.
AI.motivation: Open-loop unstable LPTV plants cannot be identified via open-loop experiments; a closed-loop framework is needed that shifts stability requirements from the plant to the internally stable closed-loop system.
AI.method: An exact algebraic plant-extraction theorem for cycled closed-loop realizations is derived, enabling recovery of the cycled plant transfer matrix from stable closed-loop maps (reference→output, reference→input) without state augmentation. A closed-loop subspace identification algorithm follows: apply subspace ID to cycled signals, extract the plant algebraically, and recover LPTV parameters via coordinate transformation.
AI.result: Numerical examples demonstrate successful recovery of stable and open-loop unstable SISO LPTV plants; MIMO validation via coordinate-invariant Markov-parameter comparisons is also shown.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method enables closed-loop identification of LPTV plants without open-loop experiments, shifting the stability burden to the closed-loop system, with the conditioning of the inverse controller path governing extraction reliability.

title: Decoupled Thrust-Axis Attitude Control Using Quaternions for Chandrayaan-3 Lunar Landing Mission
comment: 6 pages, 7 figures, Published in Indian Control Conference 2025
summary: Chandrayaan-3 mission achieved a historic milestone with its successful soft landing near the lunar south pole, highlighting the critical role of the navigation, guidance, and control (NGC) system. Navigation provided vehicle state estimates relative to the Moon center, while a polynomial based guidance scheme computed the required acceleration profile to meet terminal landing conditions. This acceleration demand was translated into total thrust magnitude and attitude commands generation. Attitude command generation involved aligning the thrust axis with the required acceleration vector and constraining rotation about the thrust axis, typically governed by mission-specific requirements. Although quaternion-based control laws are preferred for their singularity-free representation, they inherently couple all three rotational axes. This coupling can lead to undesirable interactions between guidance and control, especially during large rotations about the thrust axis, due to the quaternion shortest-path property. This paper proposes a novel quaternion-based decoupling method that enables independent thrust-axis control, mitigating guidance-control interaction and ensuring proper attitude commands generation for lander attitude control.

AI.tldr: Chandrayaan-3's successful lunar south pole landing relied on its NGC system. The paper proposes a novel quaternion-based decoupling method for independent thrust-axis control, mitigating undesirable guidance-control interactions caused by quaternion coupling in large rotations.
AI.motivation: Quaternion-based control laws, while singularity-free, couple all three rotational axes. This coupling causes undesirable interactions between guidance and control during large rotations about the thrust axis due to the quaternion shortest-path property, which can compromise proper attitude command generation for lander control.
AI.method: The paper proposes a novel quaternion-based decoupling method that enables independent thrust-axis control, separating the attitude command generation into decoupled components to mitigate guidance-control interaction.
AI.result: The proposed method mitigates guidance-control interaction and ensures proper attitude command generation for lander attitude control during large rotations about the thrust axis.
AI.conclusion: A quaternion-based decoupling approach effectively resolves the coupling issue inherent in quaternion control laws, improving the robustness of attitude command generation for planetary lander missions.

title: Real-Time Retargeting Using Controllability Boundary for Chandrayaan-3 Lunar Landing
comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, Accepted for publication in American Control Conference 2026
summary: This paper presents the real-time retargeting guidance policy developed for the Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing mission. The baseline guidance generates approximate fuel-optimal descent trajectories, while a high-level policy enables safe retargeting to alternate sites when the nominal site becomes infeasible. The retargeting strategy leverages a convex representation of the controllability boundary, allowing rapid feasibility checks and real-time target updates. To the best of the authors knowledge, this represents the first application of a data-driven retargeting framework in an operational lunar landing mission. Pre-flight simulations and Chandrayaan-3 flight results validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the real-time retargeting guidance policy for Chandrayaan-3, which uses a convex controllability boundary representation to enable safe, fuel-optimal lunar landing retargeting when the nominal site becomes infeasible. This is the first operational use of a data-driven retargeting framework in a lunar landing mission, validated by simulations and flight data.
AI.motivation: To enable safe, real-time retargeting to alternate landing sites during lunar descent when the nominal site becomes infeasible, a capability not previously demonstrated operationally.
AI.method: A baseline fuel-optimal guidance generates descent trajectories, while a high-level retargeting policy uses a convex representation of the controllability boundary for rapid feasibility checks and real-time target updates.
AI.result: Pre-flight simulations and Chandrayaan-3 flight results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed data-driven retargeting framework.
AI.conclusion: This is the first operational application of a data-driven retargeting framework in a lunar landing mission, and the approach was validated both in simulation and in actual flight.

title: Robustness Enhancement of Consensus Networks: the Optimal Memory Depth
summary: Understanding what governs collective robustness and how it can be enhanced remains a central pursuit in network science. This paper investigates the robustness of multi-agent consensus networks, quantified by the $H_2$ performance metric, and delves into the enhancing effect of agents' local memory on it. Inspired by the hierarchical temporal structure of memory observed in neuroscience, we focus on the role of memory depth, which reflects the temporal features of memory from recent to remote. Building on linear extrapolation, we propose a consensus protocol with single-step memory and tunable memory depth, derive the necessary and sufficient condition for achieving consensus, and show that the protocol exhibits an inheritable consensus property across memory depths. Furthermore, analytical expressions for the $H_2$ performance metric, which depend on the memory factor, memory depth, coupling gain, and Laplacian spectrum, are established. Under balanced usage of real-time and memory information, we demonstrate that memory at any accessible depth enhances $H_2$ performance, and the optimal memory depth occurs at either the most recent or the most remote memory, contingent upon certain parameter regions. Further detailed discussions are provided to clarify the broader implications of our findings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how local memory depth (temporal range of past information) enhances robustness ($H_2$ performance) in multi-agent consensus networks. The authors propose a single-step memory protocol with tunable memory depth, derive consensus conditions, and show that memory at any accessible depth improves robustness, with optimal depth being either the most recent or most remote memory depending on parameters.
AI.motivation: Understanding and enhancing collective robustness in networked multi-agent systems remains a central challenge in network science. The paper is motivated by hierarchical temporal memory structures observed in neuroscience, aiming to translate insights about memory depth into engineering consensus protocols.
AI.method: The authors propose a consensus protocol based on linear extrapolation with single-step memory and tunable memory depth. They derive necessary and sufficient conditions for consensus, establish analytical $H_2$ performance expressions dependent on memory factor, memory depth, coupling gain, and Laplacian spectrum, and analyze optimal memory depth under balanced usage of real-time and memory information.
AI.result: The protocol exhibits an inheritable consensus property across memory depths. Memory at any accessible depth enhances $H_2$ performance. The optimal memory depth is found at either the most recent or the most remote memory, depending on specific parameter regions.
AI.conclusion: Local memory depth demonstrably improves collective robustness in consensus networks, with the optimal memory configuration governed by system parameters. The findings have broader implications for designing more robust multi-agent systems informed by neuroscience principles.

title: Teleoperation Operational Design Domain based on Minimal Risk Maneuver Capability
comment: This is a preprint. The manuscript is under preparation and has not yet been submitted for peer review
summary: This article discusses the concept of an Operational Design Domain (ODD) designed specifically for teleoperated road vehicles. For this purpose, the ODD concept designed for automated driving is adapted for teleoperation. As teleoperation becomes more common in regular traffic, the question arises under which operating conditions such vehicles are able and allowed to drive. Currently, these conditions are selected primarily based on network performance. From a safety perspective, it is difficult to base such a selection on a reliable connection because it is almost impossible to guarantee sufficient reliability. With this in mind, the ODD concept designed for automated driving is adapted for teleoperation: A concept is proposed for basing the ODD for a teleoperation system on the capability of the teleoperated vehicle to perform a minimal risk maneuver using a dedicated system designed solely for this purpose. This concept is then demonstrated using a use case example.

AI.tldr: The paper adapts the Operational Design Domain (ODD) concept from automated driving to teleoperated road vehicles, proposing an ODD based on the vehicle's ability to perform a minimal risk maneuver using a dedicated fail-safe system, rather than relying on network reliability.
AI.motivation: As teleoperation becomes more common in regular traffic, determining safe operating conditions is critical. Current reliance on network performance for selecting conditions is problematic because network reliability is almost impossible to guarantee sufficiently from a safety perspective.
AI.method: The ODD concept from automated driving is adapted for teleoperation. The proposed approach bases the ODD on the teleoperated vehicle's capability to execute a minimal risk maneuver using a dedicated system designed solely for this purpose. A use case example demonstrates the concept.
AI.result: A concept for teleoperation-specific ODD is proposed and demonstrated via a use case example, shifting the basis from network reliability to the vehicle's own fail-safe maneuver capability.
AI.conclusion: Basing the ODD for teleoperation on the vehicle's ability to perform a minimal risk maneuver via a dedicated fail-safe system offers a more safety-robust alternative than relying on network connection reliability.

title: Distributed Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for District Heating Networks
summary: This paper presents a distributed nonlinear model predictive control that uses alternating direction method of mul tipliers for district heating networks. Exploiting a graph-based modeling of the thermal dynamics, our controller optimizes the mass flow absorption of buildings in a distributed cooperative scheme that mediates between the superior performance of the centralized control and the privacy preservation of the decentralized schemes. A benchmark three-building network simulation is used to compare the performance of the proposed solution with a decentralized model predictive control scheme.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a distributed nonlinear model predictive control using ADMM for district heating networks, optimizing mass flow absorption of buildings in a cooperative scheme that balances centralized performance with decentralized privacy. Simulation on a three-building network shows comparison with decentralized MPC.
AI.motivation: To achieve both superior control performance (like centralized schemes) and privacy preservation (like decentralized schemes) for district heating network optimization.
AI.method: Distributed nonlinear model predictive control using alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with graph-based modeling of thermal dynamics.
AI.result: The proposed distributed cooperative scheme was benchmarked against a decentralized MPC on a three-building network simulation.
AI.conclusion: The distributed MPC using ADMM mediates between centralized control performance and decentralized privacy preservation for district heating network optimization.

title: BuilDyn: Excitation-Driven Data Generation for Building Thermal Dynamics Modeling and Control
summary:
Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used for data-driven modeling of buildings to enable downstream tasks such as fault detection and diagnosis, and energy-efficient control. While recent work improves generalization across building characteristics, weather, and occupancy, generalization also depends on sufficient exploration of the control-driven system state space. Existing real-world datasets and simulation environments predominantly reflect stationary operation under fixed control policies, resulting in limited excitation and reduced robustness to unseen operating conditions.
  This paper introduces BuilDyn, a package based on BuilDa that enables customizable excitation strategies for control-oriented data generation. BuilDyn further supports sampling from representative building distributions and provides a Python interface for easy integration into machine learning pipelines. We demonstrate the benefits of BuilDyn by comparing the performance of data-driven ML models trained on non-excited and excited data for one building. With BuilDyn, we hope to advance scalable control-oriented modeling and support future directions such as transfer learning and building-specific foundation models.

AI.tldr: BuilDyn is a Python package built on BuilDa that enables customizable excitation strategies for control-oriented building data generation, supporting sampling from representative building distributions and improved ML model robustness through better exploration of the system state space.
AI.motivation: Existing building datasets and simulation environments predominantly reflect stationary operation under fixed control policies, resulting in limited excitation of the system state space and reduced robustness of ML models to unseen operating conditions. This undermines generalization for downstream tasks like fault detection and energy-efficient control.
AI.method: BuilDyn extends BuilDa with customizable excitation strategies for control-oriented data generation, supports sampling from representative building distributions, and provides a Python interface for seamless ML pipeline integration.
AI.result: Demonstrated that ML models trained on excited (BuilDyn-generated) data outperform those trained on non-excited data for a single building case study.
AI.conclusion: BuilDyn advances scalable control-oriented modeling and supports future directions such as transfer learning and building-specific foundation models.

title: Fault-Ride-Through Coordination Strategy for Offshore AC Islands with Multi-Infeed HVDC Interconnections
summary: Large-scale offshore Wind Farms (WFs) are considered key assets towards realizing a sustainable power system. These systems are often configured as offshore AC islands and their integration largely depends on the High-Voltage-Direct-Current (HVDC) technology. This topology, while it enables cost-effective transmission over large offshore distances, may lead to operational challenges. Specifically, the operation of offshore AC islands during faults and the grid code requirement fulfillment are identified as a major challenges for their large-scale deployment. To address this pressing issue, a comprehensive coordination control strategy for the different participating converters in multi-infeed AC offshore islands during Fault Ride Through (FRT) operation is presented in this work. The proposed strategy introduces advanced control functions in the FRT schemes of both the HVDC and WF converters, such as zero active and reactive power injection during faults, as well as post-fault active power droop control coordination to tackle power imbalances. The proposed FRT coordination strategy is validated through both extensive simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC, as well as with Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) experimental results, considering both AC and DC faults.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive coordination control strategy for multi-infeed AC offshore islands with HVDC integration during Fault Ride Through (FRT) operation, validated through simulations and PHIL experiments.
AI.motivation: Large-scale offshore wind farms configured as AC islands with HVDC transmission face operational challenges during faults and grid code compliance, which hinder their large-scale deployment.
AI.method: A coordination control strategy is proposed for converters in multi-infeed AC offshore islands during FRT, featuring zero active/reactive power injection during faults and post-fault active power droop control coordination. Validation is performed via PSCAD/EMTDC simulations and Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHIL) experiments under AC and DC fault conditions.
AI.result: The proposed FRT coordination strategy is validated through extensive simulations and PHIL experimental results for both AC and DC faults.
AI.conclusion: The proposed coordination control strategy effectively addresses FRT challenges in multi-infeed AC offshore islands with HVDC transmission, enabling grid code compliance and operational stability.

title: Optimization of Predictive Maintenance Schedules under Uncertainty: A Scenario-Based Theoretical Framework
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: This paper proposes a scenario-based framework for predictive maintenance scheduling under uncertainty in a finite planning horizon. The considered setting involves multiple assets for which maintenance decisions are informed by three heterogeneous sources of information: calendar-based overhaul intervals, usage-based limits driven by uncertain future operating cycles, and condition-monitoring outputs represented through remaining useful life (RUL) estimates with uncertainty. While these elements have been studied extensively in the maintenance literature, they are often treated separately or only partially integrated. In contrast, the proposed formulation evaluates complete maintenance schedules under simulated future scenarios and compares them using expected-cost and tail-risk criteria. The contribution is primarily conceptual and methodological: we define a unified finite-horizon decision framework that combines calendar-, usage-, and prognostics-based information within a common scheduling problem. A small synthetic computational example is used as a proof of concept. The results show that integrated scenario-based policies can substantially outperform simpler single-trigger rules, while the difference between risk-neutral and risk-aware integrated policies remains modest under the present calibration.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a scenario-based predictive maintenance framework integrating calendar-based, usage-based, and condition-monitoring (RUL) information sources under uncertainty, demonstrating through a synthetic example that integrated policies outperform single-trigger rules, with modest differences between risk-neutral and risk-aware approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing maintenance literature treats calendar-based, usage-based, and prognostics-based information sources separately or only partially integrates them, leaving a gap for a unified decision framework that combines all three under uncertainty.
AI.method: A scenario-based framework is developed for predictive maintenance scheduling over a finite horizon, using simulated future scenarios to evaluate complete maintenance schedules. The framework compares policies using expected-cost and tail-risk criteria, integrating multiple heterogeneous information sources.
AI.result: Integrated scenario-based policies substantially outperform simpler single-trigger rules. The difference between risk-neutral and risk-aware integrated policies is modest under the present calibration.
AI.conclusion: The proposed unified finite-horizon decision framework that combines calendar-, usage-, and prognostics-based information is conceptually and methodologically sound, as demonstrated through a proof-of-concept synthetic example.
